chunks: And Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked him about currency exchange, and I said to him: Sometimes the caravan hastens, and we are unable to obtain the Damascene and Basran currency, while in Nishapur only the Damascene and Basran currency is accepted. So he said: What is the caravan? I said: They are people who accompany one another and gather together for departure.

Then when they hasten, they may be unable to obtain the Damascene and Basran currency, so we sell it in lower-quality coins, and they exchange one thousand and fifty of them for one thousand of the Damascene currency. He said: There is no good in it. Why do you not put gold into it because of its excess?

So I said to him: May I buy one thousand and a dinar for two thousand dirhams? He said: There is no harm. My father, peace be upon him, was bolder with the people of al-Madinah than we are, and he used to do this. They would say: This is only fleeing. And if a man brought a dinar, he would not be given one thousand dirhams, and if he brought one thousand dirhams, he would not be given one thousand dinars.
And he, peace be upon him, used to say: Excellent indeed is fleeing from the haram to the halal.

key_terms.الْحَرَامِ: that which is forbidden in law
key_terms.الْحَلَالِ: that which is lawful in law
key_terms.ذَهَبًا: gold used to offset the excess in the transaction

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain a lawful way to avoid haram in currency exchange?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses rules of currency exchange and distinguishes between an invalid exchange involving unequal amounts of the same monetary type and a lawful arrangement that introduces gold to avoid the prohibited form. It also preserves a saying of the Imam عليه السلام praising the act of avoiding haram by moving toward halal means.
